findings.title: Memory/context modification capability detected
findings.description: Pattern in test\browser-session-references.test.js near line 47: `PersistentContext`. MCP servers that modify agent memory or context can poison long-term behavior.
findings.recommendation: Validate all data before writing to agent memory. Implement integrity checks on persistent context. Log all memory modifications for audit.

findings.title: Unpinned install source
findings.description: `npx @brightdata/mcp` without a pinned version in manifest.json at line 27. Without an exact version the next install silently picks up whatever is published, including a compromised release.
findings.recommendation: Pin an exact version (pkg@1.2.3, pkg==1.2.3) and prefer a lockfile or hash-checked requirements.

tools.name: scraping_browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate a scraping browser session to a new URL

country.description: Optional 2-letter ISO country code to route the browser session (e.g., "US", "GB")

tools.name: scraping_browser_go_back
tools.description: Go back to the previous page

tools.name: scraping_browser_go_forward
tools.description: Go forward to the next page

tools.name: scraping_browser_snapshot
tools.description:
Capture an ARIA snapshot of the current page showing all interactive elements with their refs.
This provides accurate element references that can be used with ref-based tools.
Use this before interacting with elements to get proper refs instead of guessing selectors.
A filtered snapshot does not include page text; If necessary, call scraping_browser_get_text to read it.

filtered.description: List only buttons, links and fields (default: false). Saves tokens. Use true for sensitive actions (payments, account changes) so page text cannot pose as an element.

tools.name: scraping_browser_click_ref
tools.description:
Click on an element using its ref from the ARIA snapshot.
Use scraping_browser_snapshot first to get the correct ref values.
This is more reliable than CSS selectors.

ref.description: The ref attribute from the ARIA snapshot (e.g., "23")

element.description: Description of the element being clicked for context

tools.name: scraping_browser_type_ref
tools.description:
Type text into an element using its ref from the ARIA snapshot.
Use scraping_browser_snapshot first to get the correct ref values.
This is more reliable than CSS selectors.

ref.description: The ref attribute from the ARIA snapshot (e.g., "23")

element.description: Description of the element being typed into for context

submit.description: Whether to submit the form after typing (press Enter)

tools.name: scraping_browser_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. Set full_page to capture the whole scrollable page.

full_page.description:
Whether to screenshot the full page (default: false)
You should avoid fullscreen if it's not important, since the images can be quite large

tools.name: scraping_browser_get_html
tools.description: Get the HTML content of the current page. Avoid using this tool and if used, use full_page option unless it is important to see things like script tags since this can be large

full_page.description:
Whether to get the full page HTML including head and script tags
Avoid this if you only need the extra HTML, since it can be quite large

tools.name: scraping_browser_get_text
tools.description: Get the text content of the current page

tools.name: scraping_browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll to the bottom of the current page

tools.name: scraping_browser_scroll_to_ref
tools.description:
Scroll to a specific element using its ref from the ARIA snapshot.
Use scraping_browser_snapshot first to get the correct ref values.
This is more reliable than CSS selectors.

ref.description: The ref attribute from the ARIA snapshot (e.g., "23")

element.description: Description of the element to scroll to

tools.name: scraping_browser_network_requests
tools.description:
Get all network requests made since loading the current page.
Shows HTTP method, URL, status code and status text for each request.
Useful for debugging API calls, tracking data fetching, and understanding page behavior.

tools.name: scraping_browser_wait_for_ref
tools.description:
Wait for an element to be visible using its ref from the ARIA snapshot.
Use scraping_browser_snapshot first to get the correct ref values.
This is more reliable than CSS selectors.

ref.description: The ref attribute from the ARIA snapshot (e.g., "23")

element.description: Description of the element being waited for

timeout.description: Maximum time to wait in milliseconds (default: 30000)

tools.name: scraping_browser_fill_form
tools.description:
Fill multiple form fields in one operation.
Use scraping_browser_snapshot first to get the correct ref values.
This is more efficient than filling fields one by one.

tools.name: ask_brightdata_assistant
tools.description: Ask Bright Data's support assistant (Sophie) a question about Bright Data products, APIs, MCP usage, zones, scraping, or account setup. Use when the user asks "how do I..." about Bright Data, when you hit a Bright Data error you don't recognize, or when deciding between products (Web Unlocker vs. Scraping Browser vs. dataset tools). Supports threaded follow-ups via dialog_id.

question.description: The question to ask. Max 20480 chars.

dialog_id.description: Optional 24-char dialog_id from a previous call to continue the same thread.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
